title: Probabilistic Race and Ethnicity Prediction Using Group-Specific Name Lists
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the use of an LLM to generate distinctive surname lists for Lebanese religious sects. These lists were then embedded and combined with geographic priors in the proposed list-powered Bayesian Improved Surname Geocoding (ℓBISG) model to probabilistically predict individuals' sectarian/religious memberships.
findings: The LLM successfully generated high-quality surname lists for various religious sects in Lebanon in Arabic. When applied within the ℓBISG methodology, these LLM-generated name lists produced accurate and well-calibrated individual probability estimates of religious sect membership, outperforming predictions based solely on geographic locality and reducing the district-level baseline RMSE by approximately 68%.
